newsitem.title: USA: Lobbyist gets subpoena over Rep. Burton allegations.
newsitem.headline: Lobbyist gets subpoena over Rep. Burton allegations.

text.p: A federal grand jury investigating campaign fund-raising has subpoenaed a lobbyist who alleged he had been "shaken down" for contributions by Congressman Dan Burton, the lobbyist's lawyer said Thursday.

Lawyer Plato Cacheris said the subpoena required that lobbyist Mark Siegel, and one of Siegel's associates, Brian Sailer, testify before the grand jury next Wednesday about the allegations involving the Indiana Republican lawmaker.

Cacheris said Siegel and Sailer were cooperating with the investigation, led by a Justice Department task force that previously has focused on the campaign fund-raising controversy involving the Democrats and President Clinton.

Siegel, a former lobbyist for the Pakistan government, alleged in a memo last July that "Burton threatened me and has now obviously attempted to interfere with my livelihood" by contacting Pakistani officials to express his anger.
According to Siegel, Burton said he wanted at least $5,000 raised for his re-election campaign from Pakistani-Americans. Siegel alleged in the two-page memo that he had been "shaken down" by Burton.

Burton has denied the allegations. Burton, the chairman of a House committee investigating campaign finance abuses, has charged the Justice Department probe represented an attempt to "discredit" and "intimidate" him.
Cacheris said Siegel, a longtime Democrat, and Sailer had been interviewed separately by the FBI Monday. The allegations involving Burton first were reported by the Washington Post last week.
Justice Department officials previously said the task force would review the allegations, but the subpoena represented a new step in the widening criminal investigation.
Cacheris said task force prosecutors were "moving quickly" and added the allegations appeared to be "of interest to their investigation."
A grand jury, consisting of 17 to 23 citizens, hears evidence and decides whether to bring any criminal charges. All of its proceedings are conducted in secret.

The grand jury Wednesday heard testimony from Florida businessman R. Warren Medoff about his talks with President Clinton and top White House aide Harold Ickes in October about a Democratic Party contribution.
Medoff said he testified about "campaign finances and a contribution regarding the president, the White House and the Democratic National Committee."

He said his testimony mainly involved his dealings with former Deputy White House Chief of Staff Harold Ickes concerning a possible contribution by a Texas business associate. The contribution never was made.
